title: Bavarian crochet square
subtitle: Concentric colour rings with front-post treble ridges worked in the round
excerpt: The Bavarian square builds outward from the centre in colour-ringed rounds, each ring locked to the previous with front-post trebles that create a raised ridge at every colour change. The post stitches pull the round inward slightly, producing a slightly domed, textured motif that photographs beautifully from above.
sourceNotes: The Bavarian stitch construction is documented in German needlework manuals from the late 19th century. The crochet adaptation appears in English in Weldon's Practical Needlework, Volume 6 (1891).
heroPrompt: A Bavarian crochet square in alternating cream and dusty teal DK cotton on a pale linen background, photographed flat from above in soft daylight. Concentric colour rings with raised post-stitch ridges at each ring boundary, 12 cm square.

crochet.gaugeText: Finished Bavarian square measures 12 × 12 cm in DK-weight cotton with a 4 mm hook.

chartDefinition.title: Bavarian crochet square
chartDefinition.caption: Each round alternates a shell section (trebles) with a post-stitch ridge (fptr). Corner ch-2 spaces at each of four corners.

glossaryTerms.definition: A treble worked around the post of the stitch below rather than into the top loops. Insert hook from front to back to front around the post. Creates a raised ridge on the right side.

content.text: The Bavarian square locks each colour ring to the previous with

worked around the tops of the previous round. The post stitches pull the fabric slightly toward the centre on each ring, creating the characteristic slight dome and raised ridges at every colour boundary.

Two colours in alternating rounds give the clearest result. Three or more colours work but require more ends to weave in. Colour A starts the magic ring; colour B works the first post-ridge round; colours continue alternating through as many rounds as needed.

attrs.title: Materials for one motif
attrs.body: About 7 g colour A and 7 g colour B in DK-weight cotton. A 4 mm hook. Tapestry needle and scissors.

content.text: Magic ring. Ch 3 (counts as first tr). 2 tr into ring. *Ch 2, 3 tr into ring.* Rep 3 more times. Ch 2. Sl st to join. (12 tr, 4 ch-2 corners.)

Join colour B. Sl st to corner sp. Ch 3. Into same sp: 2 tr, ch 2, 3 tr. *Fptr around each of the 3 side tr of round 1. Into next ch-2 corner sp: 3 tr, ch 2, 3 tr.* Rep from * around. Fptr around final 3 side tr. Sl st to join. (Corner clusters + 3 fptr per side.)

Continue alternating colours, working fptr around ALL previous-round side stitches (including fptr from earlier rounds). Corner clusters grow by 0 — only the sides grow with each round. Fasten off after round 4.
Work the overlay stitch square for a related post-stitch technique that places the overlay stitches on top of a base fabric rather than building the fabric itself.
